question:
Read the following passage and answer the questions based on the passage:

'The Movement' group was formed against the elitism of The Bloomsbury and Bohemia groups. These poets wrote ironical verses that celebrated the idea of English identity and were often immersed with nostalgia. The group included the novelist Kingsley Amis, the poet-novelist John Wain, poet-critic Donald Davie, poets Elizabeth Jennings, Thom Gunn, John Wain, D. J. Enright and Robert Conquest. The title 'the Movement' was coined by J. D. Scott, literary editor of The Spectator. This group shared antipathy towards the cultural pretensions of the Bohemian and the Bloomsbury group and in general, they had the disapproval of the elitism of the modernist writings. The writers of this group were identified by their class origins, beer-drinking and pipe smoking habits.

 

What were the reasons for the establishment of 'The Movement' group in Britain?
option_1: The oppositions were against the cultural pretensions and elitism of the Bloomsbury and Bohemian groups
option_2: Modernist elitism was advocated, and experimental writing styles were in the limelight
option_3: Romantic ideals were revived, and irony in poetry was completely rejected
option_4: Avant-garde art and radical political movements were encouraged instead
solution_text:
The correct answer is 'The oppositions were against the cultural pretensions and elitism of the Bloomsbury and Bohemian groups'.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage states: “'The Movement' group was formed against the elitism of The Bloomsbury and Bohemia groups.”

• This is reinforced elsewhere: “This group shared antipathy towards the cultural pretensions of the Bohemian and the Bloomsbury group and in general, they had the disapproval of the elitism of the modernist writings.”

• This directly supports ‘The oppositions were against the cultural pretensions and elitism of the Bloomsbury and Bohemian groups’ as the answer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Detail and inference questions in Reading Comprehension are answered by locating the exact supporting line in the passage rather than by outside knowledge, even when an option sounds generally true.

 

NOTE

• The other options either reverse the passage's stated relationship, introduce a detail the passage does not mention, or describe a related but distinct idea from what the question actually asks.

question:
Read the following passage and answer the questions based on the passage:

In the annals of human achievement, the development of the spaceship stands as a monumental testament to the ingenuity and perseverance of scientists. Unlike any other invention, spaceships have revolutionized our understanding of the cosmos, allowing us to venture beyond Earth's atmosphere and unlock the mysteries of the universe. These vehicles are not merely mechanical constructs but intricate systems composed of advanced technology, engineering precision, and sheer human determination. Spaceships require a confluence of various scientific disciplines. Aerospace engineers meticulously design the structure, ensuring the spacecraft can withstand the extreme conditions of space, including vacuum, radiation, and temperature fluctuations. Astrophysicists provide crucial insights into celestial bodies and cosmic phenomena, guiding mission trajectories and objectives. Meanwhile, biologists study how living organisms can survive and adapt to the hostile environment beyond our planet, which is crucial for manned missions. Scientists who work on spaceship development often grapple with challenges that extend beyond terrestrial experiences. The absence of gravity affects both the mechanical operations of the spacecraft and the physiological well-being of astronauts. Communication delays, sometimes spanning minutes, complicate real-time decision-making. Despite these formidable obstacles, the collective efforts of multidisciplinary teams have repeatedly demonstrated triumph over adversity, pushing the very boundaries of human exploration. As humanity stands on the cusp of deeper interstellar journeys, the collaboration between centers of research, innovation, and space agencies worldwide is more vital than ever. These centers not only foster technological advancements but also cultivate the next generation of scientists who will carry the beacon of space exploration forward.

 

Choose the option that correctly fills in the blanks in the sentence below. “Scientists who work on spaceship development often ______ with challenges...
solution_text:
The correct answer is 'grapple'.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• the verb form filling the blank must agree with the sentence's subject (singular/plural) and stay consistent with the tense already established elsewhere in the sentence — this subject-verb agreement and tense-consistency check decides the correct option.

• Applying this to the sentence, the option that fits correctly is ‘grapple’.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Grammar-based questions on a passage are solved by isolating the exact sentence or clause quoted in the question and applying the relevant rule (clause type, voice, or tense) to that specific construction.

 

NOTE

• The other options break subject-verb agreement, use an inconsistent tense, or use an incorrect verb form for this sentence.
